questions.question: Q1: Can fw-context index many source versions (commits/branches/dirty trees) and retain a deterministic, historically correct semantic view for each?
questions.evidence: src/fw_context_mcp/store_v2/worlds.py:10-11,219-307 — explicit identity chain RepositoryNamespace → SourceSnapshot → Build → World, materialized idempotently via INSERT OR IGNORE over UNIQUE(namespace_id, snapshot_id, build_identity_sha). capture_repository_identity + capture_snapshot (worlds.py:176-203) capture commit + dirty-delta digest per run. Final gate F3 (3 snapshots → 3 worlds, 3 distinct snapshots), F9 (historical state immutable after source modification: 1 states, 1 worlds unchanged), F10 (restart preserves state: 1 states, 1 worlds) all PASSED. scan_m5_state LIFECYCLE states include 'active','failed','retained','retired','superseded','unfinalized'.

questions.question: Q2: Is common semantic content indexed/stored once when reuse is proven safe (same bytes + same build context)?
questions.evidence: src/fw_context_mcp/store_v2/worlds.py:475-585 (bind_tu) binds TUs to PUBLISHED SemanticStates — never mutates state (INV-1/INV-2/INV-5, docstring lines 24-25). runner.py:794-833 invokes store_v2.admission.attempt_fast_reuse BEFORE parse; a committed hit (A8 bind success) skips parse + legacy semantic writes and runs only mandatory-minimum bookkeeping. Final gate F1 (identical bytes reused 1 semantic state, binding-level) and F5 (unchanged TU reused 1 semantic state, binding-level) both PASSED.

questions.question: Q3: Does each explicit RepositoryNamespace × Snapshot × Build retain its own semantic view?
questions.evidence: src/fw_context_mcp/store_v2/worlds.py:15-16,288-307 — UNIQUE(namespace_id, snapshot_id, build_identity_sha) constraint on snapshot_builds; _ensure_world_rows materializes one World row per (ns, snap, build) triple. worlds.py:300-304 fetches the world_id by the exact triple. Final gate F3 (3 snapshots → 3 worlds, 3 distinct snapshots) and F8 (different build flags → different semantic states, W1=1 W2=1, no shared keys) both PASSED.

questions.question: Q4: Is false semantic reuse prevented? (same bytes different meaning MUST NOT reuse)
questions.evidence: Three binding gates inside one transaction (worlds.py:475-585): gate 1 refuses unpublished targets (lines 486-500); gate 2 (A-2) refuses cross-spelling reuse for path_spelling_sensitive states (lines 501-517); gate 3 refuses conflicting state for an existing binding identity — no last-writer-wins (lines 518-538, docstring line 34). build_identity incorporates toolchain_identity + parser_salt + parser_generation + environment_digest + declared_env_salt + builder_family (worlds.py:248-263). Final gate F2 (macro change produces different binding keys: A=1 B=1 binding states), F8 (different build flags → different semantic states, no shared keys), F18 (reuse attacks: false_accept_count=0 across 3 attacks, binding-level check) all PASSED.

questions.question: Q5: Does indexing a new version approach work proportional to actual semantic TU changes, not full reprocessing?
questions.evidence: src/fw_context_mcp/indexer/_unit_processor.py:189+ implements three-tier staleness (mtime → content-hash → libclang parse) per (file, context_id). runner.py:794-833 fast-reuse admission path skips parse + legacy writes on a committed A8 hit, running only mandatory-minimum bookkeeping with FRESH hashes. manifest_lookup keyed per (tu_rel, context_id) (runner.py:613-629) so two compile actions of one file each get their own staleness record. Final gate F5 (unchanged TU reused 1 semantic state, binding-level) and F7 (A→B→A: 1 semantic state reused on return to A, binding-level) both PASSED.

questions.question: Q6: Is historical query independence from the live filesystem guaranteed? (modifying source after index doesn't change historical state)
questions.evidence: src/fw_context_mcp/store_v2/worlds.py:754-810 (capture_extra_files) stores assembly content per-World into world_extra_files so get_vector_table reads immutable indexed content, NOT live disk. worlds.py:429-472 (_insert_membership) persists file_blobs.content bytes (F3 Slice 6C-F3) and re-reads+verifies main TU source blob_sha via sha256 before storing. Historical queries resolve via PinnedQueryView over a frozen World (queryview.py:248-449); the strict read path (store_v2/query.py) is READ-ONLY (mode=ro, lines 25-28) and treats semantic_states as storage visible only through that World's bindings (§36). Final gate F9 (historical state immutable after source modification: 1 states, 1 worlds unchanged) PASSED.

questions.question: Q7: Is there a single authoritative semantic system in normal production operation?
questions.evidence: src/fw_context_mcp/config/settings.py:517-518 — v2_write_authority defaults True (v2 World finalization is the authoritative success criterion), legacy_compatibility_mode defaults False. src/fw_context_mcp/indexer/_unit_processor.py:148-167 (_legacy_compat_on) returns False in default mode. runner.py:506-524,535,582,669,997,1020,1056 gates EVERY legacy path (open_db, upsert_project, upsert_build_context, drop_fts_triggers, _store_linker_scripts, asm store_units, _run_postprocess) behind _legacy_compat; when False (default), no legacy index.db is opened, no legacy writes, no legacy postprocess. v2 World finalization is authoritative: runner.py:945-991 raises IndexIntegrityError on failed/incomplete finalize when _v2_authority. Final gate F17 (full v2 operation: index→query→restart→reindex→GC dry-run all OK, 1 worlds, no legacy DB), F23 (_legacy_compat_on() returns False in default mode) both PASSED.

All legacy DB access is inert when _legacy_compat=False (runner.py:509-524 logs 'M5 v2-only mode: legacy DB not opened'). Final gate F19 (M3B scanner: V2_NATIVE_READ=29, LEGACY_EXEC=0), F20 (M4 scanner: V2_PRIMARY=4, LEGACY_PRIMARY=0), F21 (M5 scanner: numeric_gate=PASS, all counters 0) all PASSED.

questions.question: Q9: Does GC correctly preserve shared SemanticState until ALL referencing Worlds are unreachable?
questions.evidence: src/fw_context_mcp/store_v2/gc.py:128-240 (analyze_gc) computes eligible_state_rows as states referenced by eligible Worlds AND NOT EXISTS any protected World referencing the same (state_key, state_generation) — lines 199-210. apply_gc (gc.py:243-327) re-checks refcount==0 inside the transaction before each state DELETE (lines 303-312): a state shared between an eligible and a protected World is NEVER deleted. Single BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction with rollback on BaseException (lines 272-324). Final gate F13 (shared state survived W1 collection: 1 states, 2 worlds) and F14 (all roots released → 1 states collected, 2 worlds collected) both PASSED.

questions.evidence: src/fw_context_mcp/store_v2/gc.py:115 — GC_ROOT_STATUSES = frozenset({'active','retained'}); lines 162-186 classify each world: pinned→protected, building→protected, status in GC_ROOT_STATUSES→protected, unknown→protected (fail-safe). active_build_world_ids parameter (line 131, 169-171) protects the in-progress World. mark_world_retained (lines 401-437) makes a World a GC root. questions.question: Q11: Can a failed index be retried safely?
questions.evidence: src/fw_context_mcp/store_v2/worlds.py:672-730 (finalize_world) leaves a failing world as 'unfinalized' (line 712) — never flips to active. src/fw_context_mcp/store_v2/gc.py:378-398 (mark_world_failed) sets status='failed' which is GC-eligible (GC_ELIGIBLE_STATUSES line 125) but NOT queryable. src/fw_context_mcp/store_v2/query.py:68 — QUERYABLE_WORLD_STATUS = frozenset({'active'}) only; query.py:647-651 rejects non-active worlds. A retry creates a NEW active world via the same idempotent _ensure_world_rows path. Final gate F15 (failed world not queryable, retry created new active world: 1 total) and F16 (retry after restart created new active world: 1 total, 1 active) both PASSED.

questions.question: Q12: Is the architecture free of newest-wins semantics?
questions.evidence: src/fw_context_mcp/store_v2/worlds.py:34 docstring: 'no last-writer-wins (task §22)'; binding gate 3 (lines 518-538) refuses conflicting state for an existing binding identity — returns refused_conflict, never overwrites. src/fw_context_mcp/mcp/shared/queryview.py:248-449 (resolve_current_view) is DETERMINISTIC and FAIL-CLOSED: step 3 (lines 342-349) selects active worlds for the EXACT (namespace_id, snapshot_id) ordered by world_id (stable, not newest); when multiple active worlds exist with no build_id_hint, it raises AmbiguousWorld (lines 423-436) — a storage handle NEVER chooses semantic Build identity (RISK A fix, D004). The ONLY ORDER BY world_id DESC (line 366) is gated behind allow_tree_mismatch=True (shadow-validation only, default False, lines 267-282 explicitly 'NOT safe for v2 authority'). legacy_config_hash_to_build_id (lines 454-484) uses ORDER BY sb.world_id LIMIT 1 (lowest, deterministic) as a compatibility bridge, not a semantic authority. Final gate F18 (reuse attacks: false_accept_count=0 across 3 attacks, binding-level check) PASSED.

summary: Reconstructing from current code (not cached ledgers) at HEAD bbaa6d3e6b79f0d6ef2653bbd26fc456ed6077b0, the multi-version semantic-indexing Goal is TRULY COMPLETE. The v2 store implements the full RepositoryNamespace → SourceSnapshot → Build → World → TUBinding → published SemanticState identity chain with UNIQUE constraints and idempotent INSERT OR IGNORE materialization (worlds.py). Normal/default operation is v2-only: _legacy_compat_on() returns False by default (_unit_processor.py:148-167), every legacy path in runner.py is gated behind that flag, and v2_write_authority defaults True so v2 World finalization is the authoritative success criterion. Three independent scanners (scan_m5_state, scan_authority_state, scan_write_authority) report ZERO legacy reads/writes/creations/exec/fallbacks/mirror/primary in the default path. GC is reachability-based (gc.py): GC_ROOT_STATUSES={active,retained}, pinned/building/unknown worlds are protected fail-safe, shared SemanticStates are deleted only when NO protected World references them AND a transaction-time refcount==0 check passes, all in one rollback-safe transaction. The read path is READ-ONLY and deterministic-fail-closed: resolve_current_view raises AmbiguousWorld on multiple active worlds without an explicit build_id_hint — no storage handle ever chooses semantic Build identity, no newest-wins. Failed indexes leave the World 'unfinalized'/'failed' (not queryable, GC-eligible) so retry creates a fresh active World. The end-to-end final project gate passes 23/24 clauses; the single failure (F24) is the self-referential clause requiring exactly this fresh Guardian acceptance artifact, which this file now provides. All 12 Guardian questions answer YES with HIGH confidence.
